conn = swat.CAS('example.sas.com', port=8777, username="alexal", password="password")
ERROR: The TCP/IP negClientSSL support routine failed with status 90bfc0e0.

Traceback (most recent call last):
File "", line 1, in
File "/usr/lib/python2.7/site-packages/swat/cas/connection.py", line 297, in init
raise SWATError(self._sw_error.getLastErrorMessage())

commit message: I have changed the code to add/subtract the subarray bound values as needed to get sources into the right place when doing a subarray simulation.  The XYToRADec and RADecToXY routines are for pixel positions given with respect to the full frame whereas the code is assuming that pixelx, pixely are with respect to the subarray, hence whenever pixel positions are input for sources one has to use pixelx + self.subrray_bounds[0] and pixely + self.subarray_bounds[1] to get the correct RA/Dec strings, and when RA/Dec input positions are converted to pixelx, pixely positions using RADecToXY_astrometric (or RADecToXY_manual as the case may be) one has to subtract self.subarray_bounds[0] and and self.subarray_bounds[1] from pixelx and pixely respectively.  The changes have been made wherever I see the XYToRADec or RADecToXY routines being called.

commit message:
Fix issues with installed tblis.h not being usable.

This required a number of changes:
- Move `src` directory to `tblis` so that statements like `#include "tblis/tblis_config.h"` work before and after installation.
- #include headers from marray and stl_ext using short paths and adjust include flags in the Makefile.
- Remove blis.h dependency in any user-facing include files. This necessitated hard-coding a few constants (data type enums) and forward-declaring several structures.
- Put marray and stl_ext headers in their own top-level include directories.
- Add a top-level `tblis.h` stub which just #includes `tblis/tblis.h`.

Also, add CircleCI config file for testing (including installation).

I suggest to convert them to N during the initial step.

author: Jonathan Leitschuh <Jonathan.Leitschuh@gmail.com>
commit message:
vuln-fix: Zip Slip Vulnerability



This fixes a Zip-Slip vulnerability.

This change does one of two things. This change either

1. Inserts a guard to protect against Zip Slip.
OR
2. Replaces `dir.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalPath())`, which is vulnerable to partial path traversal attacks, with the more secure `dir.getCanonicalFile().toPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalFile().toPath())`.

For number 2, consider `"/usr/outnot".startsWith("/usr/out")`.
The check is bypassed although `/outnot` is not under the `/out` directory.
It's important to understand that the terminating slash may be removed when using various `String` representations of the `File` object.
For example, on Linux, `println(new File("/var"))` will print `/var`, but `println(new File("/var", "/")` will print `/var/`;
however, `println(new File("/var", "/").getCanonicalPath())` will print `/var`.

Weakness: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
Severity: High
CVSSS: 7.4
Detection: CodeQL (https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/java/java-zipslip/) & OpenRewrite (https://public.moderne.io/recipes/org.openrewrite.java.security.ZipSlip)

Reported-by: Jonathan Leitschuh <Jonathan.Leitschuh@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Leitschuh <Jonathan.Leitschuh@gmail.com>

author: Simone Gianfranceschi <simone.gianfranceschi@intecs.it>
commit message:
Added the exchange time in the response as comment.
The format is the following <!--Response received in [XXX] milliseconds-->
The comment is included in the first tag of the response (both for HTTP exchanges as well as for SOAP)
The exchange time can be extracted with the xsl comment() command.

As an example the following xsl excerpt extract the exchange time from a SOAP message (stored in the SOAP_MESSAGE variable)

<xsl:value-of select="substring-before(substring-after($SOAP_MESSAGE//*[local-name() = 'Envelope']/comment(),'['),']')"/>

author: Simone Gianfranceschi <simone.gianfranceschi@intecs.it>
commit message:
Added the exchange time in the response as comment.
The format is the following <!--Response received in [XXX] milliseconds-->
The comment is included in the first tag of the response (both for HTTP exchanges as well as for SOAP)
The exchange time can be extracted with the xsl comment() command.

As an example the following xsl excerpt extract the exchange time from a SOAP message (stored in the SOAP_MESSAGE variable)

<xsl:value-of select="substring-before(substring-after($SOAP_MESSAGE//*[local-name() = 'Envelope']/comment(),'['),']')"/>

commit message:
Fixes for path manipulation vulnerability.
Added a ValidPath class which validates
that the path is legal before it is used.
The rules in valid path require that a path:
1) is rooted at:
    - TE_BASE
    - TE_INSTALL
    - java.io.tmpdir
    - TE_BUILD
2) does not include the string ".."
3) is not rooted at:
    - c:\Windows
    - /etc
    - /bin
    - /usr/bin

The environment variables listed in item
1 must be set or paths will not validate.

commit message:
GPU: wait for computation to finish

The output variable `summ` is stored in host memory which is legal
because the function output can be stored in host or device memory
according to the cublasXasum() documentation but the call still submits
work asynchronously to the GPU. That is, the CPU code has to wait for
the GPU code to finish (e.g., by means of a cudaDeviceSynchronize()
call) to avoid a race condition when evaluating the termination
condition.

commit message:
Add an assert macro

FYPP copies the C pre-processor closely including all of its pitfalls:
if you use the statement `if(not .${cond}$)` as suggested in the FYPP
documentation, your code will break with expressions as simple as
`x == 1 .or. x == 2` because this expands to

  if(not x == 1 .or. x == 2)

or equivalently

  if((not x == 1) .or. (x == 2))
